personal.name: Charlie De Buriatte
personal.title: IT Support Specialist
personal.headline: I start with the simple checks and keep going until the fault makes sense.
personal.tagline: Most of what I know came from fixing real faults, at work and in my home lab.

bio.short: IT Support Specialist with Tier 1-2 support experience at VantageUAV and a home lab I keep building on. Building expertise through hands-on projects and continuous learning.
bio.medium:
I like IT support for the moment something finally works and the person can get back to what they were doing. I enjoy the figuring-it-out part, working through a fault step by step until it makes sense, but the best bit is seeing the stress lift for the other person. More and more people have started coming to me with their tech problems, and being trusted with that means a lot.

The fix I remember best from VantageUAV was a colleague who couldn't send or receive email. I started with the simple checks, then tried Outlook on the web. That worked, so the account was fine and the fault was in the desktop app. I found Microsoft's Inbox Repair Tool, ran it, and their email was syncing again.

I'm proudest of this portfolio. The first version had every AI giveaway going: heavy gradients, emojis everywhere, stock phrasing, everything stacked dead centre. It looked finished but felt shallow. Since then I've learned to steer AI tools instead of accepting the first output, and I've replaced the filler with my own words and photos. It taught me that the skill is knowing what good looks like and spotting when the output isn't it.
bio.full:
I became genuinely interested in technology in my early teens, starting as a typical user before gradually becoming the person who fixed things. Gaming, building PCs, and experimenting with virtual machines sparked a deeper curiosity about how systems actually work beneath the surface. Over time, that curiosity turned towards understanding how it works and building it myself.

Although I originally considered paths like healthcare or history, I found myself increasingly drawn to systems, infrastructure, and problem-solving. Building my own environments and troubleshooting real hardware issues, including diagnosing instability linked to Intel's 13th generation platform, strengthened my interest in technical problem-solving and persistence.

More recently, the rapid evolution of AI reignited that same curiosity. What began as casual experimentation evolved into using AI tools to build practical projects and improve workflows. Today, I'm focused on developing strong IT fundamentals while continuing to explore how modern tools, including AI, can enhance real-world systems and operations.

projects.title: Job Application Analyser
projects.tagline: Privacy-first web app that scores your CV, then writes your cover letter
projects.description: Upload your CV, paste in any job description and you get an instant match score from weighted scoring algorithms. Then Claude AI writes a tailored cover letter ready to send, plus CV bullet suggestions aimed at that job. Scoring runs in your browser. Only the cover letter step sends text to Anthropic, using your own API key.
projects.long_description:
Job Application Analyser helps job seekers make objective decisions about which positions to apply for and take action faster. Built with privacy as a priority: scoring happens in your browser and there is no backend storing anything. When you generate a cover letter, your CV and the job text go straight to Anthropic using your own API key.

The weighted scoring algorithm treats required skills as 3x more important than preferred skills and includes 12 tool equivalency groups, so knowing Freshdesk counts for Zendesk, Jira experience covers Trello and Asana, and AWS counts towards Azure and GCP roles.

v3.0.0 adds full Claude AI integration: paste a job description, run the analysis, then hit Generate to get a tailored cover letter in your personal voice and structure, plus specific CV bullet points grouped under the exact section they belong in. The first formal GitHub release marks the app as stable and publicly usable end-to-end.

Claude AI CV bullet suggestions: grouped by section so you know exactly where to paste them
Selective AI generation: toggle cover letter and CV suggestions independently

Weighted scoring algorithm (required skills 3x preferred)
12 tool equivalency groups: Freshdesk counts for Zendesk, Jira covers Trello/Asana/Monday, AWS covers Azure/GCP
ITSM/ITIL equivalency: Service Desk and Helpdesk experience counts for framework labels

Application tracker with pipeline stages: Saved → Applied → Interview → Offer / Rejected

Search and filter history by title, company, or pipeline status
Export full application history as CSV
Recurring skill gaps: bar chart of skills missing across recent analyses
Keyword suggestions: one-click copy of missing skills as bullet points
Shareable results links: compressed URL anyone can open to see your full results
PWA: installable on Android and iOS, opens full-screen, works offline

projects.title: Hjelply: Community Support Platform
projects.tagline: Full-stack mutual aid network with points economy and trust progression
projects.description: A full-stack community platform that connects people who need help with people who can give it. It runs on a points-based economy with escrow, a 5-tier trust progression system and a complete admin moderation panel. Paused for now while I focus on higher-priority projects.
projects.long_description:
Hjelply is a demonstration mutual aid network designed for individuals who need flexible peer-to-peer support. Users can both request and offer help: posting tasks, earning points, and building trust through a structured reputation system.

The name is a placeholder with a nice ring to it, inspired by the Norwegian word for help ('hjelp'), courtesy of a Norwegian girlfriend. Built to explore the real complexity behind fair exchange systems, user trust, and accessible UI design for a sensitive user group.

5-tier trust progression system (online-only → home access)
Task posting, management and matching
Rating, review and dispute resolution system
Admin moderation panel
Emergency and urgent task flagging

Mobile-responsive across all pages

projects.title: Intel 13th Gen Platform Investigation
projects.tagline: Stutters, crashes and random blue screens that everything said was the graphics card. It wasn't.
projects.description: Games started stuttering badly and crashing, and I was getting blue screens with a different error every time. It turned out to be the Intel 13th gen instability problem, fixed by a microcode update in the motherboard BIOS.
highlights: Assumed it was the graphics card. Updated the drivers, then wiped them with DDU and reinstalled, then reseated the card. No change
Swapped in my old GTX 1070 Ti. Same problem, so the GPU was ruled out
The blue screens never showed the same error twice. Researching that turned up reports of an Intel 13th gen microcode fault, but I put it down to a few unlucky CPUs and moved on
Checked temperatures and the cooler mount in case the CPU was overheating. While monitoring, I noticed the CPU voltage didn't look right
Started crashing in Disney Dreamlight Valley too, so it wasn't one game. Went back to the 13th gen reports and my symptoms matched
Checked MSI's BIOS page almost hourly for the fix and installed it as soon as it came out
projects.side_text: Stable since the BIOS update went on.
projects.why_built: To resolve persistent stability issues and develop advanced hardware diagnostic skills.
challenges_solved: Identifying root cause among conflicting information
Systematic isolation testing
Documentation and analysis of non-standard symptoms
Structured troubleshooting approach
projects.impact: Strengthened analytical thinking and diagnostic methodology for complex hardware issues

projects.title: Outlook Not Sending or Receiving
projects.tagline: Outlook on the web worked fine. The desktop app didn't. That told me where to look.
projects.description: At VantageUAV a colleague couldn't send or receive email in Outlook. I worked through the simple checks, used Outlook on the web to rule out the account, then repaired Outlook's local data file with Microsoft's Inbox Repair Tool.
highlights: Fully closed Outlook, including its background processes, and reopened it
Checked the internet connection was stable
Checked whether Microsoft had any known Outlook issues
Tried Outlook on the web. It worked, so the account was fine and the fault was in the desktop app
Suspected the local mailbox file was damaged, looked up Microsoft's repair tool and found SCANPST.EXE in the Office folders
Ran it once, and Outlook started syncing again
projects.side_text: Sending and receiving again after a single repair, and my colleague was back to normal.
